consumer_seed: The Ofcom text-relay guide was published on 26 September 2014.
Ofcom requires landline and mobile telephone companies to provide specified services for customers with disabilities.
One required service is access to an approved text-relay service for people with hearing or speech impairments.
Text relay provides text-to-speech and speech-to-text translation.
A relay assistant acts as an intermediary between the parties to a telephone call.
Ofcom approves text-relay providers and sets minimum service standards.
Next-generation text relay can be accessed using mainstream equipment including PCs, laptops, tablets and smartphones.
Next-generation text relay supports simultaneous voice, hearing and text.
An internet-connected device is required to benefit from all next-generation text-relay improvements.
A hearing- or speech-impaired user makes a text-relay call by dialling 18001 followed by the destination number.
Using text relay on a smartphone or computer requires the free relay app.
A standard landline or mobile can carry the voice part while an internet-connected device displays the text.
A TextNumber is a standard 11-digit number that automatically brings the relay service into a call.
Relay calls are charged at the same rate as standard telephone calls, subject to the customer's package.
The Ofcom emergency-video-relay guide was published on 31 March 2023.
Emergency video relay enables deaf British Sign Language users to call UK emergency services in their first language.
Emergency video relay requires a connected device such as a smartphone, tablet or computer and can be accessed through the 999BSL website or app.
Emergency video relay is available 24 hours a day.
Emergency video relay is free to use.
999 BSL calls have the same priority as voice 999 calls and are answered by the same emergency control-room staff.
A caller's location is normally provided to emergency services during an emergency-video-relay call.
Emergency video relay is staffed by qualified and experienced interpreters.
The emergency-video-relay obligation came into force on 17 June 2022.
The obligation covers providers of internet-access services and technically feasible number-based interpersonal communications services to end users.
Regulated providers must provide emergency video relay free of charge and, where technically feasible, apply an incremental price of zero to associated data traffic.
The regulated service must be available 24/7, support BSL video relay and provide a text channel alongside video.
